rationale: This is a very small C++ OOP benchmark (215 lines, 15 functions, ~2 KB of text) dominated by tiny virtual-dispatch display() methods, so size-inflating passes are the main threat to acceptable overhead. SUB is nearly free and disrupts arithmetic constants throughout, so it gets the strongest security/diversity weights with minimal cost penalties. SPLIT is similarly cheap and adds useful structural diversity to the larger functions (programmer/consultant/secretary display at 350-440 bytes). BCF is penalized heavily on size and runtime because bogus basic blocks explode tiny member functions with little analytic payoff at this scale, and FLA is similarly discouraged on size though kept moderately relevant since flattening the few larger functions still hinders control-flow recovery. IBR retains decent security/diversity value but carries high runtime weight given indirect-branch overhead on hot small methods, and ICALL is kept moderate since the program's virtual dispatch already obscures call targets and added indirection mainly costs runtime. IGV is the riskiest pass for a 15-function interprocedural program with a plausible vtable-driven call graph, so its CorrectnessRisk weight is set high to make the compiler apply it only where features clearly justify it.
